sentences.text: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE GAUTAM KUMAR CHOUDHARY

-----
For the Appellant : Mr. S.K. Deo, Advocate For the State : Mr. B. Shastri, APP

-----
Oral Order 05 / Dated : 15.02.2024  Heard the parties.
1. The judgment of conviction under Section 354 of Indian Penal Code and order of sentence to undergo rigorous imprisonment for six months is under challenge in the instant criminal appeal.

2. The prosecution case in brief as set out in the F.I.R lodged by the prosecutrix is that on 17.03.2007 in the afternoon at 14:30 hours while she was going from her home to the brick kiln taking lunch for her husband, she was intercepted by the appellant who attempted to commit rape with her on the point of knife.
On Hulla her husband came there, and on his approach the appellant fled away from the place of occurrence.
Madhupur Kairo P.S. case No. 27 of 2007 was registered under Sections 376 and 511 of Indian Penal Code against the appellant.
3. The police after investigation submitted charge-sheet and after cognizance the accused was put on trial under Sections 376 and 511 of Indian Penal Code.
4. Altogether six witnesses were examined including the prosecutrix and relevant documents have been adduced into evidence marked as exhibits.

5. The trial Court returning the judgment of conviction by recording a finding that the appellant had attempted to outrage the modesty of the victim lady and sentenced the appellant to six months of imprisonment under Section 354 of Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text: 6. The judgment of conviction and order of sentence has been assailed on the ground that no independent witness has come forward to support the prosecution case.
There is no medical evidence to show that the prosecutrix has suffered any injury in attempted rape.

It is also argued that the appellant has a Grocery shop and there was a due of Rs.49,000/- and in order to misappropriate the amount, instant false case has been filed.
7.

Learned counsel for the State has defended the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence and submitted that there is no delay in institution of FIR which was lodged on the very next day of the incidence.
The prosecutrix has given a consistent account regarding the incidence in her testimony as PW3.
The place of occurrence was a desolate place between the house of the prosecutrix and brick kiln where she was going to deliver lunch to her husband.
Taking advantage of her being alone, attempt to rape was committed.

8. Having considered the submissions advanced on behalf of both sides and the evidence on record,
it is evident that there is no material to show that the prosecutrix was actuated with desire to falsely implicate the appellant in the incidence.
The defence has failed to confront the prosecutrix with her re- statement made to the police or the FIR to elicit any contradiction.
She has given consistent account in the cross-examination at para 8, regarding the manner of incidence.
Her account is duly corroborated by her husband who has been examined as PW2.
PW1 Fagu Mirdha, who happened to be the brother-in-law of the prosecutrix, has also supported the case.
I do not see any reason to doubt any testimony on account of these witnesses.
The judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the trial court needs no interference.
The appeal is dismissed and the appellant's bail is cancelled.
He is directed to surrender before the court below within two weeks to serve the remaining part of sentence.
(Gautam Kumar Choudhary, J.) AKT/Satendra Uploaded Naresh Yadav vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116590918/
